title: TokenCake: A KV-Cache-centric Serving Framework for LLM-based Multi-Agent Applications
technique: agent-aware KV cache management: temporal scheduler (proactive offload of idle KV during function calls, predictive upload) and spatial scheduler (priority-based memory partitioning reserving memory for critical-path agents)

optimized_metrics.stat_quote: average latency by up to 47.06% compared to vLLM

optimized_metrics.evidence: To mitigate temporal ... underutilization, the Temporal Scheduler uses an ... opportunistic policy to proactively offload the KV ... Cache of stalled agents during function calls
to reserve memory for critical-path agents (§5).

headline_claim.text: TokenCake reduces end-to-end latency by up to 47.06% in memory-constrained settings and improves effective GPU utilization by 16.9 percentage points compared to vLLM.

reported_metrics.where: Fig 9 (average app latency vs QPS), Fig 13-15

metric_definitions.definition_quote: We report end-to-end latency (average and tail percentiles) from application submission to final response, and GPU KV Cache utilization as the fraction of KV Cache blocks occupied over time.
metric_definitions.notes: Application-level (multi-agent DAG, including function-call stall times), not a single LLM call. Tool durations replayed from recorded distributions for fairness.

metric_definitions.definition_quote: Some agents lie on the critical path, meaning any delay they experience directly increases the total time-to-result for the entire application.
metric_definitions.notes: Motivates reserving memory for critical-path agents; app latency is determined by the DAG critical path.

metric_definitions.definition_quote: GPU KV Cache utilization as the fraction of KV Cache blocks occupied over time
metric_definitions.notes: Per the text, the useful quantity is blocks allocated to active, computation-ready requests (not idle stalled agents).

load_regime: request (application) arrival-rate sweep, Poisson arrivals in QPS (0.2-1.0 QPS etc.), memory-constrained settings via gpu_mem_utilization
tradeoff_acknowledged: Plain agent-agnostic offload reduces total latency but less than TokenCake; offload noise/mispredicted tool time reduces gains (14.8% with zero noise); priority_first policy gives lowest mean latency but inflates tail (first_fit chosen for best tradeoff); offload adds overhead.
hardware: A100 80GB, H20 96GB (x1 and x2 TP), 100GB CPU offload memory
workloads: Code-Writer (11 agent types) and Deep Research multi-agent applications; ShareGPT and AgentCode inputs; Poisson app arrivals
extractor_notes: End-to-end latency is application-level (submission to final response), so PROGRAM_JCT, not request-level. No TTFT/TPOT.
